title: Legal detriment and surrender of freedom
shortTitle: Legal detriment and surrender of freedom
summary: A legal detriment occurs when a person gives up a legal freedom or assumes an obligation as part of an exchange. It can exist even when the choice benefits that person.
notes:
In Hamer, abstaining from drinking and tobacco could improve the nephew’s health while restricting his legal freedom. The court therefore rejected an inquiry limited to whether the nephew was worse off in an everyday sense. Identify the right surrendered or obligation undertaken, then connect that act to the requested exchange. An act that simply follows a promise, without being bargained for, requires a separate reliance analysis.

Hamer rejects the assumption that consideration must make the promisee worse off in a financial or health sense. The surrendered ability to act supplies the relevant legal change when requested as part of the bargain. The same chapter cautions that a detriment merely happening after a promise is not sufficient: the promisor must have sought it in exchange.
